headline: French quantum computer maker Quobly now has access to a European chip pilot line run by research institute CEA-Leti to develop its silicon-based quantum processors.
score_reason: Partnership extension with concrete access, but no results or funding; press-release based.
importance_line: It helps a European company working to build quantum chips with standard silicon manufacturing, which matters to the regional chip industry, though Quobly's computer is not yet on sale.
source: DQ India, carrying a CEA-Leti and Quobly announcement
summary: DQ India reports a CEA-Leti and Quobly announcement that Quobly, which builds quantum computers from silicon spin qubits (qubits stored in the spin of an electron in silicon), can now use the FAMES Pilot Line, a European test line for advanced chip making. Quobly also works with STMicroelectronics on 300 mm wafers and plans to commercialise its first quantum computer, Alloy Pioneer, by the end of 2026.
